Photograph: SWNS View image in fullscreen A woman is arrested in Covent Garden after the stabbings. Photograph: SWNS UK news Woman arrested after four men stabbed in London’s Covent Garden Metropolitan police say 47-year-old woman arrested on suspicion of possession of offensive weapon and assault Covent Garden stabbings – latest updates Caroline Davies and Helena Horton Wed 5 Aug 2026 12.42 EDT First published on Wed 5 Aug 2026 09.47 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A woman has been arrested after four men were stabbed in Covent Garden, central London, police said. The Metropolitan police said the men, aged 34, 39, 42 and 52, were found with stab wounds. They were taken to a major trauma centre after the lunchtime incident on Endell Street. Two of the men were being treated for injuries that were not believed to be life-threatening or life-changing and the other two had been discharged. A 47-year-old woman remained in custody after being arrested on suspicion of possession of an offensive weapon, believed to be a pair of scissors, and assault. Ch Supt Jason Stewart, who leads policing in the area, said: “Officers responded within minutes of this incident after receiving a number of reports. While still at an early stage of the investigation, we would like to reassure the community that we currently believe this to be an isolated, mental health-related incident. “A visible police presence will remain in the area while evidence is gathered at the scene and we thank the public for their understanding.” A London ambulance service spokesperson said: “We sent an ambulance crew, a paramedic in a fast-response car and an incident response officer. We also dispatched London’s air ambulance. We treated four patients at the scene and took them all to a major trauma centre as a priority by road.” map of Covent Garden One witness said the stabbing happened outside the Shaftesbury Theatre before the woman allegedly made her way down Endell Street, a popular location for eating and drinking in the area. The witness, who wanted to remain anonymous, said: “We noticed she stabbed three people with scissors by the theatre then she came down here and the police were here.” One of the victims ran into a barber shop and took his shirt off, revealing a large gash in his back, workers there said. Arjan Gjorga, who works at the Rock and Sole Plaice restaurant and witnessed the attack, said a woman involved in the incident was known to people who worked on the street. He said: “I see her all the time, she’s a homeless person. She walks up and down asking for help, she visits the church at the top of the street.” Gjorga, who did not have to close his restaurant, said: “We all saw a commotion, people were running away. It was totally random, just random people. She suddenly started stabbing them. The police reacted immediately, they arrested her right away.” View image in fullscreen Emergency services near the scene on Endell Street in Covent Garden. Photograph: James Manning/PA Matt Bishop, 42, who works at a consultancy firm next to the cordon in Covent Garden, said he had seen a woman having a “standoff” with three police officers and waving a weapon around. Andrea, the manager of Da Mario restaurant on the same street, said the attack happened in the middle of lunch service. Gesturing at a pair of men enjoying cocktails on the shaded terrace, he said: “They saw it all but they weren’t fazed. They had a police cordon right over their heads but they kept on enjoying their lunch. It’s just another day in London.” He also recognised the alleged perpetrator, saying: “She’s often on the street. We’ve seen her do things like this before, she’s recently got in an argument with a mate and thrown a bottle of vodka on the floor and it smashed outside the restaurant.” By 3.30pm, the area was calm with the cordon down. Europe Hungary Expels 10 Russian Diplomats Russia said the move would be met with a ‘harsh and painful’ response. Save Mark Us Preferred on Google Print Hungarian Prime Minister Peter Magyar in Budapest, Hungary, on July 13, 2026. Tamas Purger/MTI via AP Guy Birchall 9/8/2026 | Updated: 9/8/2026 0:00 X 1 Hungary ordered the expulsion of 10 Russian diplomats on Sept. 7. Moscow’s ambassador to Budapest was told that “according to the assessment of the Hungarian authorities, 10 members of the Russian mission had engaged in activities in Hungary that are unacceptable for diplomats under the Vienna Convention,” Foreign Minister Anita Orbán said in a Sept. 8 post on X. The Vienna Convention is a 1961 treaty that governs diplomats’ behavior. “This decision protects Hungary’s security and sovereignty,” Orbán continued, adding that it “does not imply breaking off diplomatic relations with Russia,” and that Budapest “intends to continue the necessary dialogue, based on mutual respect and adherence to the rules.” She did not provide any more details, including as to how long the banishment would last. Russian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova told Moscow’s state news agency TASS that the Kremlin’s response to“the Russophobic lobby in Budapest will be harsh and painful.” Related Stories Hungary Declares Russia a Threat, Reversing Orban’s Moscow-Friendly Policy Ukraine–Russia Hostilities Resume After Witkoff, Kushner Visit Hungary’s move was praised by the European Union, which has voiced support for the new government since former Prime Minister Viktor Orbán was ousted in an election earlier this year. European Commission spokesperson Christian Wigand said Budapest made a “legitimate decision,” which he characterized as “an expected reaction in view of Russia’s persistent campaign in using hybrid attacks against the EU and its member states.” He added that the EU expresses its “full solidarity” with Hungary and “reaffirms its support for the diplomatic and consular activities of all member states conducted in accordance with international law,” saying that the 27-nation bloc would “continue to coordinate with Hungary and other member states and remains committed to protecting the interests and rights of EU citizens.” Hungary’s move comes just days after Germany ordered the shuttering of the Russian consulate in Bonn and the Russian House in Berlin on Sept. 1 after blaming Moscow for an attempted drone attack on Leipzig/Halle Airport in August. It also builds on a reversal of Hungary’s position on Russia. Last month, Budapest declared Moscow a “threat to the global order” and formally condemned its military aggression, a sharp shift in the new government’s outlook compared with that of its predecessor. Policy guidelines published on Aug. 25, which must be followed by Budapest’s delegation to the 81st session of the U.N. General Assembly, stated that “Hungary condemns the Russian military aggression and fully supports Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity within its internationally recognised borders, and recognises Ukraine’s right to self-defence.” Hungarian Prime Minister Peter Magyar has pushed more anti-Russian policies since taking office, moving Hungary away from the previously cozy relationship it had with the Kremlin under Viktor Orbán and toward more affable terms with the rest of the European Union, which it joined in 2004. So far, Magyar has announced a review of Orbán’s 2014 Paks II nuclear power plant deal with Russia’s Rosatom, secured a deal to release 16.4 billion euros ($19.1 billion) in frozen EU funds, and rescinded Budapest’s vetoes on reimbursing EU countries for arms sent to Kyiv. He also returned gold and cash that Budapest had seized from bank vehicles that were transporting the assets across Hungary to Ukraine. Despite Magyar cooling Budapest’s relationship with Moscow, his government remains opposed to fast-tracking Ukraine to membership in the EU, which will entail some EU-required reforms on Ukraine’s part. “Hungary continues to oppose accelerated EU accession. If Ukraine succeeds in closing all 33 accession chapters within the next 10 to 15 years, Hungary will support Ukraine’s accession, subject to a legally binding referendum,” Magyar said in a June 3 post on X. Under Viktor Orbán, who is unrelated to the current foreign minister, Hungary maintained much more friendly relations with Moscow than most other nations in Europe in the wake of the Kremlin’s invasion of Ukraine. The former prime minister repeatedly blocked EU sanctions packages against Russia during his tenure, was a vociferous opponent of Brussels’s plans to ban Russian energy imports, and made multiple trips to Moscow to meet with Russian President Vladimir Putin. https://www.dw.com/en/nigerian-military-.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5NnDH The plane involved in the crash is similar to the one in the picture (FILE: August 10, 2026) Image: Steven Mohr/SNS/picture alliance Advertisement Nigerian authorities on Tuesday revised the death toll from a military aircraft crash in southern Nigeria to 25, down from the 32 initially reported, and said there were no survivors. "NAF 931 had 25 persons on board, comprising five ‌crew members and 20 passengers," Nigerian ​Air Force (NAF) said ‌in ​a statement. Nigerian President Bola Tinubu extended his "deepest condolences" to the deceased's loved ones. The aircraft was on a routine mission to Lagos, Nigeria's economic hub, when it crashed in the Igbokoda area of Ondo state, Aviation Minister Festus Keyamo said in a statement. Wreckage located Keyamo said the aircraft disappeared from radar at around 9 a.m. local time (7:00 a.m. GMT) and was later found to have crashed about halfway through its journey from Edo state to Lagos. He said the wreckage had been located near a naval base. The Nigerian Air Force identified the aircraft as an ATR-42 and said an immediate search and rescue operation had been launched. A video circulating on social media showed a small crowd gathered near a river as rescuers searched the area by boat. Locals told AP news agency about what they had heard and seen. "The plane cleared some trees. We found some body parts, some clothes and shoes," one of the locals said. UPDATE: The initial version of this story on Monday, October 5 had the death toll at 32, as reported by Nigerian officials. This has been amended following the updates on Tuesday. https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c5ly.text: Image source, Getty Images By Anthony Zurcher North America correspondent Published 5 hours ago Donald Trump's decision to import Russian fuel to the US represents a remarkable about-face from the president. Just three weeks ago, Trump signed legislation to authorise fresh American sanctions and tariffs on nations that import Russian oil and gas. Now, Trump says, Russian President Vladimir Putin has agreed to supply hundreds of thousands of tons of diesel fuel to the US and world markets in the coming months. The deal comes as Trump is still grappling with the political fallout of the Iran war and its impact on global energy prices, weeks before American voters head to the polls in the midterm elections. As the cost of fuel has skyrocketed in America, his standing with the public â stung by the higher prices at the pump and knock-on effects that led to across-the board inflation â has soured. The toll the war is taking has been acutely felt by US agricultural states, which rely heavily on diesel to operate farming machinery and to transport their products to market. It is these states â places like Iowa, Kansas, Texas and Ohio â that have become unexpected political battlegrounds in the upcoming elections that will determine if Republicans maintain control of Congress. Trump announces deal for Russian diesel as Zelensky criticises 'gift to Putin' Published 2 hours ago What are the US midterms? A simple guide Published 4 days ago For months, the American president has been searching for ways to ease his party's political pain. He recently pressured European allies to further tap their oil reserves . He deferred federal taxes on the fuel and authorised supplies designated for farm use to be used in interstate trucking. He has also promised that he would not renew attacks on Iran until after the midterms â an unusually frank acknowledgement of the political impact the ongoing conflict is having. His decision to strike a deal with Russia's Putin is only the latest, most dramatic effort. Trump's Truth Social posts often provide incomplete information, of course. The details of exactly how Russia is supplying this fuel to the global market, and what they might get for in return â besides much-needed hard currency â is unclear. It opens Trump to criticism from European allies and American politicians that his administration is now helping to fund the Russian war machine. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky called the deal a "gift" to Putin that Russia would "repay" with "terror and perfidy". "Allowing Russia to sell petroleum products is an investment in a war that must be ended, not prolonged," he wrote on X. It is also uncertain exactly how much Trump's move will help Republicans at the ballot box. The promised European diesel release hasn't moved energy prices significantly, and there's no information on the speed with which Russian fuel could enter the market. Its diesel refinery capacity has been damaged by repeated Ukrainian strikes â attacks that Trump has encouraged Zelensky to curtail. The US uses approximately 3.6 million barrels of diesel a day, so even if Russia delivers its promised 300,000 tons this month, that amounts to approximately half of the US daily consumption. Americans may not notice much of an immediate difference. With less than a month before November's midterm elections, early voting has already started in many states. The political cake, as the saying goes, is all but baked. "Lower prices for Americans, especially our Great Farmers, Ranchers, and Truckers, is my Greatest Priority," Trump wrote in his Truth Social post. But over the past seven months, prices on energy, fuel and consumer goods have only gone up - even as Trump and his officials have repeatedly assured an uneasy public a successful resolution to the war, and an easing of its economic impact, is nearly at hand. Trump may be left hoping that his latest deal, setting aside its potentially uncomfortable diplomatic issues, will be enough to convince American voters that his promise of impending economic relief is more than just empty words. Minutes later 10 other men, their faces covered with ski balaclavas, came down the street on foot pursued by a police van. Soon after Emmanuel Macron’s televised speech on Sunday night telling the nation it was “unbearable to see our streets ransacked”, groups of men looted shops in central Paris for hours for a second night running. Dozens of people attempted to smash windows near Les Halles shopping centre and grab goods. https://24.hu/kulfold/2026/11/09/krakkoi.text: Hétfő reggelre meghalt a krakkói merénylő, Michal Oksinski , aki hat embert ölt meg a lengyel város főterén, és sokakat megsebesített, köztük két rendőrt is. Mielőtt november 7-én, szombaton délután a krakkói főtérre behajtott a kocsijával, és ott válogatás nélkül tüzelni kezdett a járókelőkre, a 24 éves támadó feltehetően az otthonában végzett a saját szüleivel és a húgával is. A tragédia miatt Lengyelországban kétnapos nemzeti gyászt rendeltek el. Donald Tusk miniszterelnök pedig a felhívta a politikusok figyelmét arra, hogy ne használják ki a saját céljaikra az esetet. Ám a kormányfő felhívását éppen csak a legérintettebbek hagyták figyelmen kívül. A sort a kormányfő saját belügyminiszterével, a centrista-baloldali kormány tagjával, Marcin Kierwinskivel kezdhetjük, aki a lövöldözés után nem sokkal arról beszélt : „minden jel arra mutat, hogy a merénylő nagyon radikális nézeteket vallott” és „szélsőjobboldali ideológiák” vezérelték. Kierwinski a legerősebb kormánypárt, a centrista Polgári Platform tagja, tehát Tuskkal azonos táborhoz tartozik. Mindezek után a lengyel jobboldal a belügyminisztert kezdte támadni. Jaroslaw Kaczynski volt miniszterelnök, a legnagyobb ellenzéki párt elnöke, a Tuskék előtt hosszú ideig kormányzó, nacionalista-populista Jog és Igazságosság (PiS) nevű szerveződés vezére szerint egy zavarodott elméről van szó az elkövető esetében. Kaczynski szerint – akit az egyik legnagyobb lengyel hírportál, az Onet.pl idéz – ezért a krakkói főtéren lövöldöző férfinek az ideológiai háttere vagy politikai nézetei irrelevánsak, azaz nem játszottak szerepet a támadás elkövetésében. Tarjányi Péter biztonságpolitikai szakértő óvatosan áll ahhoz a közléshez, hogy a krakkói merényletet automatikusan szélsőjobboldali támadásnak nevezzék. „Kizárni persze nem lehet ezt” – mondta a 24.hu-nak, hiszen nincsenek a médián kívüli információi a támadóról. Ugyanakkor a szakértő szerint van egy olyan körülmény, amelyik más irányba terelheti a vizsgálatot. Ez pedig az, hogy a támadó feltehetően megölhette – legalábbis a nyomozás eddigi adatai szerint – a családját.
